title: Track restart-required per output component instead of only globally
why: UiStatus's docstring already reserves a restart_required value, but only a single global _restart_required flag exists today (mediainfo/configui/output.py), flipped by any outputs.* edit - a user editing one output has no way to tell which specific display actually needs restarting.
what: Extend restart tracking from ConfigStore.save_form's single global flag to record which specific outputs.* config paths changed since the last restart, then thread that through to UiComponent.status.
notes:
2026-07-23 dispatched to background agent `a129971bd99527f17`
2026-07-25 Implemented per-output-type restart tracking, additive to the existing global _restart_required flag. ConfigStore.save_form/save_raw/restore_backup now return a third value, changed_output_types: FrozenSet[str] - save_form returns exactly the OUTPUT_CONFIG_TYPES keys actually merged from the posted outputs dict (matches the client's existing one-output-type-per-save flow); save_raw/restore_backup conservatively return every registered output type (they can rewrite the whole file with no per-field provenance), mirroring their existing 'assume a restart might be needed' reasoning for the global flag. ConfigUiOutput accumulates these into a new in-memory self._restart_required_outputs: Set[str], cleared by /api/restart alongside _restart_required. Threaded into ui_builder.build_components()/_output_components(), which now sets each output UiComponent.requires_restart from membership in that set (was hardcoded True for every output) and status to the (now-implemented) 'restart_required' value via _status_for's new parameter, ranked below disabled/needs_configuration but above health-derived status. UiModel's UiStatus comment updated to drop the stale 'not derivable per component' note. Global UiDashboard.restart_required and the Restart button are unchanged (save_form's blanket bool computation kept, just decomposed by type). One deliberate edge-case narrowing, not exercised by any test: previously bool(outputs) counted an all-unknown-output-type payload toward restart_required; now only recognized+merged types count. Truth-grounding: background/context in the prompt matched the code as found exactly, no discrepancies. Verification: ruff check --fix mediainfo (clean), ruff format mediainfo (145 files unchanged), mypy mediainfo (Success: no issues found in 145 source files), pytest tests/test_config_ui.py tests/test_ui_model.py (215 passed). Test coverage for this mechanism is explicitly deferred to roadmap task 004 per the task's own chain description, not added here. Decision doc: docs/foreman/001.md.

title: Consolidate config UI nav from 11 items back down by nesting Pipeline under Dashboard and History under Library
why: H5 unified the config UI nav specifically to fix users losing their mental map, but History and Help (both added since) brought the sidebar back up to 11 top-level items, re-fragmenting the exact thing H5 fixed.
what: Nest Pipeline as a tab/section inside Dashboard (client-side routing only, dashboard.js renderSection()) and History as a tab inside Library, dropping two entries from NAV_SECTIONS/dashboard.html without removing either feature. Also reconsider whether Help needs a full nav slot versus a footer icon next to Theme/Hitster-safe.

title: Sort or badge commonly-used plugins ahead of niche ones on Media/Metadata/Displays pages
why: 18 sources / 19 enrichers / 15 outputs all render as one unsorted, unbadged list, so a fresh install looks equally complex to a Kodi-only household and a Kodi+Sonos+HA+Plex one.
what: Add a lightweight commonly-used/popular marker (or a configured-first default sort) to the card grid in components.js so a new install's Media/Metadata/Displays pages surface likely-relevant plugins first instead of one flat alphabetical list of 15-19 cards.
